newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somali group accuses Ethiopian troops of invading.
newsitem.headline: Somali group accuses Ethiopian troops of invading.

text.p: A Moslem fundamentalist Somali group on Friday accused Ethiopian troops of invading western Somalia and seizing the border town of Dolow after two days of fighting.

Ahmed Bile Hassan, a member of the executive committee of the al-Ittihad al-Islami (Islamic Union), said Dolow was seized by Ethiopian troops and tanks on Tuesday and two Islamic fighters were killed.

There was no immediate comment on the report from Ethiopia. Aid workers said they could not confirm the report but added that Dolow had been virtually deserted since Ethiopian troops briefly seized it during an incursion into western Somalia in August.
Hassan accused Ethiopian troops of pushing 20-km (12-miles) into Somalia and setting up a base in Dhusay village while hundreds of people were fleeing nearby towns held by al-Ittihad.
Dolow, 500-km (300-miles) southwest of Mogadishu was one of three towns seized by Ethiopian troops in a two-day incursion into western Somalia in August to hit Moslem fundamentalist bases.
But Ethiopia said it might have to hit what it called the "multinational terrorist group" in Somalia again in the future.
